title: Hormuz maritime incident risk: crude tanker struck off Oman
net_new_delta: UKMTO reported a crude-oil tanker struck by an unidentified projectile about 4 nautical miles east of Oman. Crew safe and no environmental impact reported. This is material physical-maritime event evidence but does not establish Strait closure or petroleum-flow loss.

FACT: UKMTO reported a crude-oil tanker was struck about 4 nautical miles east of Oman; crew were safe; no environmental impact was reported.
SOURCE_CLAIM: UKMTO described the projectile as unidentified; attribution is not established.
MODEL_INFERENCE: Promote HORMUZ_MARITIME_INCIDENT_RISK as an event-risk state while keeping REALIZED_ENERGY_SUPPLY_DISRUPTION unconfirmed.

affected_assumptions: Geopolitical headlines alone are insufficient to represent Gulf energy risk; physical maritime incidents should be a distinct intermediate state before realized flow disruption.
conflicts: Physical maritime risk is confirmed, but available evidence does not establish casualties, environmental damage, Strait closure, or petroleum-flow loss.
next_decisive_check: Require UKMTO/JMIC or shipping-data confirmation of additional attacks, traffic reduction, rerouting, freight/insurance repricing, or measurable oil/LNG-flow impairment; then require corresponding crude/refined-product confirmation before promoting to REALIZED_SUPPLY_DISRUPTION.

evidence.title: Crude oil tanker struck by unknown projectile off Oman, UKMTO says

oracle.finding: Add HORMUZ_MARITIME_INCIDENT_RISK as a distinct event-risk state; do not promote realized energy-supply disruption without measurable shipping or physical-flow impairment.

supermesh_x.finding: Reuters/UKMTO confirms the incident but not attribution or flow impairment; keep incident, attribution, shipping-flow, freight/insurance and market-price channels separately provenance-tagged.
